newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1997 inflation target hard to miss - Belka.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1997 inflation target hard to miss - Belka.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Wednesday that a quick reduction of the inflation rate in the first months of 1997 made the budget's target of 13 percent price growth this year difficult to miss.

"After three months and from what we see during the first half of April, we can expect progress in pulling down inflation during the first half of the year to be so great that it will be difficult not to achieve 13 percent (in December)," Belka told the Panorama television news programme.
In March, year-on-year consumer price inflation fell to year-on-year 16.6 percent, down from 17.3 percent in February and 18.5 percent in December of last year.
A Reuter poll of leading Polish banks released last week showed the year-end inflation forecast at about 15.7 percent.
